I have farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. My father taught me, and now I just do what worked last year and watch what my neighbors do.

For wheat, I plant in October. I use improved seed, the kind in the red bag from the dealer in town — my neighbor Lao Zhang used it last year and his wheat looked good. I plant about 15 jin per mu. Before planting, I spread one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I top-dress with half a bag of urea per mu, about 25 jin. The dealer told me 20 jin is enough, but two years ago I used 20 jin and my yield was lower than Lao Zhang's, so now I use 25 jin. I irrigate 3 times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once at jointing in April, and once when the heads come out in May. I spray pesticide twice — herbicide once right after planting, and insecticide once in spring for the aphids. I hire Old Wang's tractor for rotary tillage, 50 yuan per mu.

For maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in June. Everyone in my village plants this, it is reliable. I use about 3 jin per mu. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, same as wheat. Then when the maize is knee-high at big trumpet stage, I add half a bag of urea, about 20 jin per mu. I irrigate twice: once after planting if there is no rain, and once at tasseling in August. I spray 3 times: herbicide once at planting, and insecticide twice because the corn borer comes every year.

Fertilizer is expensive now, over 100 yuan per bag. But in 2021 I tried to save money and used only half a bag of compound per mu, and my wheat yield dropped by almost 100 jin. That cost me much more than the fertilizer. So now I always use one full bag per mu. Better to waste a little fertilizer than lose the crop. My wife and I do all the spraying and fertilizing ourselves. For harvest I hire the combine. I expect about 450 kg per mu for wheat and 550 kg per mu for maize. If the weather is good like two years ago, maybe 50 kg more.
